# Sorting Algorithm

#### Course: Learn Java Intermediate

## Sorting Algorithm

Suppose we have an ArrayList with elements 999, 212, 333. And we want them to be sorted in ascending order.

Instead of writing whole coding logic to sort it, we can simply use the sort() method to sort them.

```java
1import java.util.ArrayList;
2import java.util.Collections;
3
4class Main {
5    public static void main(String[] args) {
6
7        // create an ArrayList
8        ArrayList<Integer> numbers = new ArrayList<>();
9
10        // add elements
11        numbers.add(999);
12        numbers.add(212);
13        numbers.add(333);
14        System.out.println("Unsorted ArrayList: " + numbers);
15
16        // sort the ArrayList
17        Collections.sort(numbers);
18        System.out.println("Sorted ArrayList: " + numbers);
19
20    }
21}
```

Output

```text
Unsorted ArrayList: [999, 212, 333]
Sorted ArrayList: [212, 333, 999]
```

Here, we have used the Collections.sort() method to sort all the elements of the arraylist.

To use this method, we have imported the Collections package.

```java
import java.util.Collections;
```
